metadata.creator: Supreme Court of the United States
metadata.description:
Case name: Lawyer v. Department of Justice

Opinion filed: 1997-06-25

Docket No.: 95-2024

Citations:
• 138 L. Ed. 2d 669
• 117 S. Ct. 2186
• 521 U.S. 567
• 1997 U.S. LEXIS 4034

Case holding summaries:
• "[A] settlement agreement subject to court approval in a nonclass action may not impose duties or obligations on an unconsenting party or `dispose' of his claims."
• special elections must be held when district boundaries are changed, disrupting staggered Senate terms
• noting that, under Florida law, "the Attorney General as the chief law officer of the state and absent express legislative restriction to the contrary, may exercise his power and authority in the premises [the power to litigate] as the public interest may require"
• "Foremost among the factors commending the proposed resolution in this action is the consent of Florida's Senate and House . . ."
• "[P]roposed District 21, like present District 21, is primarily a legislative action and is advanced . . . by this court preeminently for that reason" (emphasis added)
• "Plan 386 passes any pertinent test of constitutionality and fairness"
• finding a community of interests as predominantly urban andlow-income even though the district crossed the Tampa Bay
• affirming district court's decision upholding constitutionality of voting district based on low income
